summary: Stefan Baums is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of Washington (2001–2009). He held posts at the University of Copenhagen, the University of Munich, and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Stockholm University in 2009 under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm. He was later a postdoctoral fellow at the University of California, Berkeley.

Stefan Mario Maul is a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Göttingen and Free University of Berlin. Since 1995 he has been Ordinarius for Assyriology at Heidelberg University, also leading research at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences.

Stefania Travagnin is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor of religion in Asia at the University of Groningen from approximately 2013 to 2020 before joining SOAS University of London.

Stefano Zacchetti (1968–2020) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned his BA and PhD at Ca' Foscari University of Venice under Alfredo Cadonna. He held professorships at Soka University and the University of Oxford.

Steffen Döll is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned his MA and doctorate at the University of Munich. After serving as an assistant at Munich, he became Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.

Stella Kramrisch (1896–1993) was an art historian and Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna. She taught at the University of Calcutta, Visva-Bharati University, and served as Professor of South Asian Art at the University of Pennsylvania.

Sten Konow (1867–1948) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Richard Pischel at the University of Halle. He served as Government Epigraphist for India and held professorships at the University of Oslo and the University of Hamburg.
Stephan Beyer is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (attested 1977).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Oberlin College, Stanford University, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry. She served as a professor at the University of Vermont from 1991 to 2015.
Stephanie Roemer is a Tibetologist who completed her doctoral studies under the supervision of Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist who completed her doctoral work at Yale University under Stanley Insler and Warren Cowgill. She taught at Harvard University and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA in 2002.
Stephen A. Murphy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who completed his MA at SOAS University of London and conducted doctoral research under the supervision of Elizabeth Howard Moore.

Stephen Addiss (1935–2022) was an art historian and scholar of Japanology who studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. He served as professor of art history at the University of Kansas and held a professorship at the University of Richmond.

Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher who studied under Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim. He led Sharpham College from approximately 1992 to 1999 and joined the core faculty of Bodhi College around 2015.

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who conducted Fulbright research at the University of Kelaniya and the University of Colombo. He has served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University.

Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religion who earned his degrees at Oberlin College and Princeton University. He has spent his career at Princeton University, where he became D. T. Suzuki Professor in Buddhist Studies.

Stephen Fuchs (1908–2000) was an Indologist and anthropologist who studied under Wilhelm Schmidt and earned a PhD from the University of Vienna. He lectured at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and founded the Anthropos Institute and the Institute of Indian Culture.

Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University under Jacqueline I. Stone. He held a post at Western Michigan University starting around 2003.
